title: What reclassification is
description:
Reclassification is the reverse of declassification: a document that was public — or was never classified — is pulled back behind the wall. It happens through executive orders, agency programs, and quiet removals.

This database documents reclassification events themselves — what was public, when it was pulled, and what the public record says about why. It never reproduces reclassified contents.

title: Executive Order 13292 (2003)
description:
EO 13292 (2003) amended the classification system to explicitly permit reclassification of previously declassified records — reversing the prior presumption against it. The order's text is public; its application created the modern reclassification era.

Policy made the pullback legal; watchdogs made it visible.

title: The NARA reclassification audit (2006)
description:
In 2006, the National Security Archive revealed — and the New York Times reported — that intelligence agencies had secretly reclassified thousands of pages at the National Archives, pulling public documents from open shelves. NARA's audit confirmed it; an MOU then required public notice of withdrawals.

The public learned its archives had been quietly edited.
